entries.original_title: Correspondence of the brain's functional architecture during activation and rest
entries.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.description: Correspondence between resting state and task brain networks
entries.citation_sentence: In the present study, these Smith et al. main findings were highly reproducible using the HCP task and resting state data.
entries.notes: The authors explicitly state the Smith et al. findings were 'replicable' and call it a 'true replication.' The replication uses different data (HCP COPE maps and resting-state ICA maps) and different analysis inputs (real task activation maps vs. BrainMap pseudo-activation maps), but preserves the core paradigm (group ICA + spatial cross-correlation of rest and task networks), warranting 'close experiment.'
